name: The Tattered Standard
region_detail: A secluded clearing within an older tract of woodland, away from regularly traveled roads.
site_type: cemetery | Ancient sites; abandoned infrastructure | Military burial ground dating to the War of Broken Banners.
history: During the final years of the war, northern soldiers buried their dead in a sheltered clearing beyond the principal military roads. Graves were marked with unworked stones and pieces of regimental cloth. A low memorial was constructed at the center of the clearing before the surviving soldiers moved on.
current_state: The burial ground remains largely undisturbed. Veterans occasionally visit to replace cloth markers and clear the graves. The central memorial bears signs of earlier repairs, and conflicting accounts among former soldiers describe an iron chest buried beneath it. No recent excavation is evident.
inhabitants: Occasional northern veterans; woodland wildlife. No permanent garrison or established undead inhabitants.
danger_level: Low ordinarily; potentially moderate if a visiting group believes the graves are being desecrated.
points_of_interest:
Simple graves; faded regimental cloth; central stone memorial; fragments of an old standard; woodland approach; a sheltered place used by visitors to kindle small fires.

Unresolved elements: The identities of the soldiers buried in the clearing; Whether the iron chest exists and what it contains; Which veterans know the directions encoded in the marching song; Whether the site becomes a rallying point or remains a private place of remembrance.
discovery: A secluded clearing within an older tract of woodland, away from regularly traveled roads. A Galrothe marching song preserves directions to the clearing. Veterans sympathetic to the Last Colours may recognize its significance and know the route.
related_records:
Rumor: R-TH-016 — The Last Colours’ Burial Ground — Direct. The clearing and purported buried chest are the subject of the rumor.
Faction Plot: P-006 — The Banner Unfurled — Potential. The memorial and any surviving records may acquire political significance if former northern soldiers begin assembling under their old banners.

Notable individuals and factions: Edric Vale (N-030) — may know the history of the burial ground or recognize the names of those interred; Former soldiers of the northern armies, including members of the Last Colours.
